extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for examiners (and applicants) on when a rejection may be made final, when finality must be withdrawn, time-for-reply (shortened statutory period) rules, advisory actions, examiner amendments, and transitional after-final practice under 37 CFR 1.129.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality when relying on art submitted in reply under 37 CFR 1.105
rubrics_metrics.description: Where information is submitted in a reply to a requirement under 37 CFR 1.105, the examiner may NOT make the next Office action relying on that art final unless all instances of the application of such art are necessitated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant submits information in reply under 1.105, any Office action that relies on that newly-submitted art must not be made final unless the rejections based on that art are necessitated by an amendment. This prevents finalizing rejections that depend on applicant-supplied art unless the amendment itself made such rejections unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make subsequent final rejection on prior art not of record against amended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or any subsequent action on the merits ... should not be made final if it includes a rejection, on prior art not of record, of any claim amended to include limitations which should reasonably have been expected to be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims were amended to add limitations that ought reasonably to have been claimed, the examiner should avoid making a subsequent Office action final when relying on prior art not of record; this protects applicants who amend to supply omissions that would prompt a reasonable new rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of common ownership statement on 102(e)/103 rejections (post-11/29/1999 applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying any 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 references against the claims of an application filed on or after November 29, 1999, the examiner should anticipate that a statement averring common ownership at the time the invention was made may disqualify any patent or application applied in a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 based on 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a common-ownership statement is filed in reply and the claims are not amended, the examiner may not make the next Office action final if a new rejection is made. See MPEP § 706.02(l)(3) for further treatment. Examiners must account for possible disqualification of references due to ownership assertions before finalizing rejections based on those references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner caution where applicant fails to point out patentable novelty in amended case
rubrics_metrics.description: In the consideration of claims in an amended case where no attempt is made to point out the patentable novelty, the examiner should be on guard not to allow such claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not indicate the patentable novelty when amending, examiner should scrutinize and may finally reject claims if, in the opinion of the examiner, they are clearly open to rejection on grounds of record. See MPEP § 714.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form Paragraph 7.40 when finality is necessitated by amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.40 should be used where an action is made final including new grounds of rejection necessitated by applicant’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶ 7.40 text: 'Applicant’s amendment necessitated the new ground(s) of rejection presented in this Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.' Includes reminder of extension of time policy (37 CFR 1.136(a)) and instructions regarding shortened statutory periods. Do not use in reissue litigation cases or reexamination proceedings as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form Paragraph 7.40.01 for IDS-with-fee necessitating final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.40.01: Applicant’s submission of an information disclosure statement under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p) on [date] prompted the new ground(s) of rejection presented in this Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when an IDS (with fee) timely prompted the new ground(s) of rejection. Examiner Note: don't use if another new ground (not necessitated by amendment) was introduced by examiner; bracket instructions for inserting filing date of IDS; not for reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a first-action final rejection is proper (continuing/substitute applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of a new application may be finally rejected in the first Office action in those situations where (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or a substitute for, an earlier application, and (B) all claims ... are drawn to the same invention claimed in the earlier application, and (2) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make a first-action final if the continuing/substitute application contains material presented in earlier application after final rejection or closing because new issues were raised or new matter was present; not proper for CIPs with new subject matter. A request for an interview prior to first action should ordinarily be granted. Use form paragraphs 7.41 or 7.41.03 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.41: Action Is Final, First Action
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.41 text: identifies the application as continuation or substitute of an earlier application and states 'THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action in this case. See MPEP § 706.07(b).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert either 'continuation' or 'substitute' in bracket 1. Examiner notes: cannot be used if amendment was refused entry in the parent on grounds of new issues or new matter; not for reissue litigation or reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.41.03: First Action following 37 CFR 1.53(d) CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.41.03: 'All claims are drawn to the same invention claimed in the parent application prior to the filing of this Continued Prosecution Application under 37 CFR 1.53(d) and could have been finally rejected on the grounds and art of record. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action after the filing under 37 CFR 1.53(d).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph is for a first-action final rejection in a Continued Prosecution Application filed under 1.53(d). Must be preceded by appropriate transitional form paragraph(s) as indicated in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prematureness of a final rejection must be raised while application pending
rubrics_metrics.description: Any question as to prematureness of a final rejection should be raised, if at all, while the application is still pending before the primary examiner. This is purely a question of practice ... It may therefore not be advanced as a ground for appeal ... It is reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prematureness is a procedural matter to be addressed during prosecution (petition under 1.181), not on appeal to the Board. Raise promptly while application pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality on examiner reconsideration when final was premature
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on request by applicant for reconsideration, the primary examiner finds the final rejection to have been premature, he or she should withdraw the finality of the rejection. The finality ... must be withdrawn while the application is still pending. The examiner cannot vacate the final rejection once the application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form paragraph 7.42 when withdrawing the finality of the rejection of the last Office action. Withdrawal must occur prior to abandonment; cannot be retroactively vacated after abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on withdrawing a non-premature final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered ... it should not be withdrawn at the applicant’s or patent owner’s request except on a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b). Further amendment or argument will be considered in certain instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible post-final amendments: those placing application in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal; amendments complying with objections/requirements as to form (37 CFR 1.116(a)). Examiner may withdraw a final rejection if new facts/reasons convince examiner claims are allowable or in reexamination where patentability changed. Withdrawal to apply a new ground is limited — typically only where a new reference fully meets a claim or differences are completely obvious. Do not use withdrawal for subsidiary, cumulative, or merely better references. When withdrawing final rejection, amendments filed after final are ordinarily entered. New grounds opened after an appeal brief require SPE approval (MPEP § 1002.02(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting of shortened statutory period (SSP) and variable reply periods
rubrics_metrics.description: All final rejections setting a 3-month shortened statutory period (SSP) for reply should contain one of form paragraphs 7.39, 7.40, 7.40.01, 7.41, 7.41.03, or 7.42.09 advising applicant that if the reply is filed within 2 months ... the shortened statutory period will expire at 3 months ... or on the date the advisory action is mailed, whichever is later. In no event can the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the required form paragraph is omitted, the SSP will end 3 months from date of final action and cannot be extended except by petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a). If an advisory action is mailed after a timely first reply, the examiner should vacate the original SSP and reset the period according to Office policy (see Notice 'Procedure for Handling Amendments Under 37 CFR 1.116').

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties when first reply filed within 2 months (advisory action possibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the final Office action sets a variable reply period ... AND applicant files a complete first reply to the final Office action within 2 months ... the examiner must determine if the reply: (1) places the application in condition for allowance; (2) places application in condition for allowance except for matters of form which examiner can change without authorization; or (3) does not place the application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (1) or (2), process as allowance and no extension fees due; if (3), issue advisory action informing applicant that the SSP expires 3 months from date of final rejection or mailing date of advisory action whichever later, by using PTOL-303 or Form Paragraph 7.67.01. Use PTOL-303 (Advisory Action form) when appropriate; otherwise use form paragraph 7.67.01 on advisory actions where a first complete reply filed within 2 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.67.01: Advisory after final when first reply filed within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.67.01: 'The shortened statutory period for reply expires THREE MONTHS from the mailing date of the final rejection or as of the mailing date of this advisory action, whichever is later. In no event ... will the statutory period for reply expire later than SIX MONTHS from the mailing date of the final rejection.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph in advisory actions where: it was the FIRST reply to the final rejection, the reply was filed within two months, and not for reexamination proceedings. Follow with form paragraph 7.41.01 if transitional provisions apply. See examiner notes for use when notice of appeal filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph 7.67.02: Vacating/reseting SSP when no variable SSP was set
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.67.02: Used when 'the first reply to the final Office action was filed within TWO MONTHS ... and the advisory action was not mailed within THREE MONTHS ... the THREE-MONTH shortened statutory period for reply set in the final Office action is hereby vacated and reset to expire as of the mailing date of this advisory action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 7.67.02 when final did not set a variable SSP but applicant filed a first reply within two months and the advisory cannot be mailed within three months. Cannot reset to later than six months from final. Any extension fee is calculated from mailing date of advisory action. Do not use if final had set a variable SSP; otherwise use 7.67.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of reply periods and extension fee timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When an advisory action properly contains either form paragraph 7.67.01 or 7.67.02, the time for applicant to take further action (including the calculation of extension fees under 37 CFR 1.136(a)) begins to run 3 months from the date of the final rejection, or from the date of the advisory action, whichever is later. Extension fees cannot be prorated for portions of a month. In no event can the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if applicant replies within 2 months and examiner mails advisory before end of 3 months, SSP expires at 3 months from final. If advisory mailed after 3 months, SSP expires on date advisory is mailed and extension fees calculated from that date. If petition for extension granted, due date computed from date on the Office action with final rejection (see MPEP § 710.01(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendment rules when first reply filed within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has been filed within 2 months of the final Office action, an examiner’s amendment to place the application in condition for allowance may be made without the payment of extension fees even if the examiner’s amendment is made more than 3 months from the date of the final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner’s amendment may not be made more than 6 months from the date of the final Office action (application would be abandoned by operation of law). If a complete first reply was not filed within 2 months, authorization for amendments placing case in condition for allowance must be within the 3-month SSP or within an extended period obtained by petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Examiner’s amendments correcting only formal matters identified for the first time after a reply would not require extension fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time (37 CFR 1.136(a)) procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requires a petition for an extension and the appropriate fee provided for in 37 CFR 1.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may file the petition and fee or give authorization to the examiner to make the petition of record and charge a specified fee to a deposit account. Office employees may not accept oral (telephonic) instructions to complete credit card forms or otherwise charge patent process fees to a credit card. When authorization is given, it must be made of record in an examiner’s amendment by indicating the person authorizing, when, deposit account number, length of extension, and fee amount. Form Paragraph 13.02.02 should be used for telephone-authorized extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and consideration of replies after final (general practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies after final should be processed and considered promptly by all Office personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies after final should not be considered by the examiner unless they are filed within the SSP or are accompanied by a petition for an extension of time and the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.17 and 1.136(a)). This applies to supplemental replies filed after the first reply. Interviews may be conducted after expiration of the SSP but within the 6-month statutory period without payment of an extension fee. Formal matters first identified after a reply and requiring applicant action may be required in an Ex parte Quayle action with no extension fees. If prosecution is to be reopened after a final Office action has been replied to, withdraw finality to avoid abandonment and extension fees (e.g., begin Office action with statement withdrawing finality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional after-final practice under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant in an application ... that has been pending for at least two years as of June 8, 1995 ... is entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits after final rejection if the first submission and the fee set forth in § 1.17(r) are filed prior to the filing of an appeal brief and prior to abandonment of the application. The finality of the final rejection is automatically withdrawn upon the timely filing of the submission and payment of the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A second submission and fee may be similarly filed prior to filing an appeal brief and prior to abandonment. The section does not apply to applications filed after June 8, 1995, or to reissue/design/reexamination proceedings. 'Submission' includes IDS, amendments to specification/claims/drawings, new substantive argument, or new evidence. Use form paragraph 7.41.01 to notify applicant that application qualifies under 37 CFR 1.129(a). Where an amendment was timely filed without the 1.17(r) fee, examiners may consider the amendment in expedited manner per MPEP § 714.13 and issue advisory actions about entry; applicant may pay fee later to obtain entry as a 1.129(a) submission. Form paragraph 7.42.01 should be used to notify applicant that finality has been withdrawn in transitional cases.
